blocks.content: Mizoram's very high forest cover (Chapter 1) supports a rich biodiversity profile, with Phawngpui (Blue Mountain) National Park as the state's flagship protected area.

cells: Named for the state's highest peak; known for its unique high-altitude flora, including rhododendrons and the rare Blue Mountain iris
Notable for its rich biodiversity, including several rare bird and mammal species
Mizoram's principal tiger reserve, part of India's Project Tiger network, though tiger sightings have been rare relative to some other reserves

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Dampa Tiger Reserve is Mizoram's designated Project Tiger reserve — a frequently tested protected-area fact, alongside Phawngpui National Park (named after the state's highest peak) and Murlen National Park (Champhai district, near Myanmar).

items: Deforestation and soil erosion linked to traditional jhum cultivation (Chapter 6) on Mizoram's steep hill slopes has been a longstanding environmental concern, directly motivating the state's New Land Use Policy shift toward settled horticulture.

Despite this, Mizoram continues to maintain one of the highest forest-cover percentages of any Indian state, a fact the state government has actively highlighted in recent public communications alongside its ongoing afforestation and biodiversity-conservation initiatives.
Phawngpui (Blue Mountain) National Park = named for Mizoram's highest peak; unique high-altitude flora.
Murlen National Park (Champhai district) and Dampa Tiger Reserve (western Mizoram, Project Tiger network) are other key protected areas.
Jhum cultivation-linked deforestation/erosion is a longstanding environmental concern, addressed via the New Land Use Policy (Chapter 6).
